threats.title: PID reuse or identity substitution
threats.precondition: A process exits or changes while ARP observes it.
threats.impact: Evidence is attributed to a different process.
threats.prevention: Bind every process to PID plus creation time and available boot or file identity.
threats.detection: Re-read identity before emitting a Proof and return PROCESS_IDENTITY_CHANGED on mismatch.
threats.residual_risk: Some platforms expose fewer identity fields without additional privilege.

threats.title: Artifact changes during observation
threats.precondition: A file is replaced or modified while it is read.
threats.impact: The digest describes inconsistent bytes or the wrong artifact.
threats.prevention: Read stable file handles and compare identity and metadata before and after hashing.
threats.detection: Return ARTIFACT_CHANGED_DURING_READ instead of a partial match.
threats.residual_risk: User-space observation cannot prevent every hostile kernel or filesystem behavior.

threats.title: Root escape through paths or links
threats.precondition: An expectation or filesystem entry contains traversal, symlink, junction, or reparse behavior.
threats.impact: ARP reads outside the declared payload or discloses unrelated files.
threats.prevention: Resolve beneath approved roots, reject traversal and non-regular types by default, and recheck targets.
threats.residual_risk: Platform namespace features require adapter-specific hardening.

threats.title: Cross-platform path normalization collision
threats.precondition: Two paths become equal after Unicode, separator, or Windows case normalization.
threats.impact: Different files produce ambiguous or non-portable tree identities.
threats.prevention: Create normalized and platform collision keys before digesting.
threats.residual_risk: Filesystems may add undocumented normalization behavior.

threats.title: Unbounded local scan denial of service
threats.precondition: A declaration selects a very large, cyclic, slow, or hostile tree.
threats.impact: ARP consumes excessive time, memory, file handles, or I/O.
threats.prevention: Enforce file, byte, duration, input, and concurrency limits.
threats.detection: Return ARTIFACT_SCAN_LIMIT_EXCEEDED and report the active bounds.
threats.residual_risk: A small number of pathological filesystem operations may still be slow.

threats.title: Execution while discovering host configuration
threats.precondition: A host configuration supports shell expansion, dynamic tags, or executable code.
threats.impact: Read-only discovery causes arbitrary local side effects.
threats.prevention: Use data-only parsers and never evaluate or launch discovered entries.
threats.residual_risk: A parser dependency may have its own vulnerabilities.

threats.title: Disclosure of local secrets or identifying paths
threats.precondition: Process, configuration, or file metadata contains credentials or private paths.
threats.impact: Proof output or logs reveal recoverable sensitive information.
threats.prevention: Apply the privacy registry before serialization and prohibit raw environment, argv, contents, and transcripts.
threats.detection: Run secret and absolute-path scanners over fixtures, logs, Proofs, and release assets.
threats.residual_risk: A digest can still act as a fingerprint when an attacker already knows candidate values.

threats.title: Pressure to elevate for stronger evidence
threats.precondition: The OS denies process or file evidence.
threats.impact: ARP broadens access or changes host security posture.
threats.prevention: Never request administrator or root rights; make indeterminate evidence explicit.
threats.residual_risk: Some protected runtimes remain unverifiable in v1.

threats.title: Untrusted or ambiguous expectation
threats.precondition: An attacker supplies a declaration that names their own bytes as expected.
threats.impact: A match is misread as supply-chain trust.
threats.prevention: Record source kind, locator hash, trust, and ambiguity independently from artifact equality.
threats.detection: Emit EXPECTATION_UNTRUSTED or EXPECTATION_AMBIGUOUS without elevating trust.
threats.residual_risk: ARP v1 does not create publisher identity or remote attestation.

threats.title: Proof mutation after observation
threats.precondition: Stored or transmitted Proof JSON is edited.
threats.impact: Consumers act on evidence ARP did not emit.
threats.prevention: Canonicalize the Proof body and bind it to proof_id with SHA-256.
threats.detection: Recompute proof_id before use and reject mismatch.
threats.residual_risk: An unsigned digest does not prove who created the Proof.

threats.title: Witness or MCP stdout protocol corruption
threats.precondition: ARP writes diagnostics or alters proxied bytes on stdout.
threats.impact: The local Agent loses the MCP session or receives changed messages.
threats.prevention: Reserve stdout for protocol bytes and send every diagnostic to stderr.
threats.detection: Compare direct and Witness byte streams and test malformed or cancelled sessions.
threats.residual_risk: A child process can itself violate the MCP transport contract.

threats.title: Witness child survives its owner
threats.precondition: The parent exits, is killed, or loses stdin unexpectedly.
threats.impact: Old runtime code continues running without supervision.
threats.prevention: Use owned Unix process groups and Windows Job Objects with bounded shutdown escalation.
threats.detection: Acceptance tests assert no child remains after every terminal path.
threats.residual_risk: A deliberately detached child outside the owned group cannot be reclaimed safely.

threats.title: Acceptance fixtures contaminate formal user state
threats.precondition: Tests reuse user homes, processes, receipts, or Agent configuration.
threats.impact: Results become ambiguous and user data is modified.
threats.prevention: Use task-owned roots, synthetic identities, bounded subprocesses, and explicit cleanup.
threats.detection: Compare pre/post state and require zero test residue.
threats.residual_risk: A crashed test runner may require task-root cleanup on the next run.
